text: Doctors should speak at the appropriate time. Patients come to the doctor to describe their symptoms, and the doctor should inform them, not question them in return. If I knew, why would I come to the doctor? I could just stay home and treat myself. And then you're talking about education regarding medical certificates? My existing medical license doesn't allow me to get one, but other doctors can. I've attended regular check-ups, but you know what? I'm here for a check-up, not to be lectured about my rights. If you don't want it, that's it. I took time off work to see a doctor, get medication, and rest. I didn't want to be lectured by a doctor. If I go back to my old job, I'll just get sick again, and how will I ever recover? Are you suggesting I quit? And you didn't even inform me of my symptoms before prescribing medication. Whether it's allergies or a cold, who would want to treat me like that? Go to another clinic that's better equipped to provide good service. I don't even want to give you one star. And this isn't the first time!

text: Today was an absolutely appalling experience. My partner needed treatment for tonsillitis, and while past medical care has always been excellent, the service was unacceptable. The credit card machine wasn't working, yet the receptionist insisted the problem was my card. After repeated attempts, it became clear the issue was their machine, not my bank. I had a stomachache for a day, but didn't have diarrhea. I went to work as usual, taking a nap and resting until I got off work. On the second day, I went to the doctor because the pain wasn't going away and I had diarrhea 6-7 times within 2 hours after waking up. The doctor asked what I had eaten that day. I told him I had salmon and yen ta fo. After listening, he told me to wait outside. I asked if I could specify on my medical certificate that I could take just one day off. The doctor insisted that I wait outside, in a softer voice, which we call a "second voice." In the end, he wouldn't let me take the day off, but I couldn't handle it. When I came back, I had diarrhea again. In short, I was absent for no reason at all.
